title: New Inventory Part has Description then Part Number, with no library pick
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Use a part number for a new part, part A, that no part or Part Library entry uses yet.
  • Start on the Inventory page (Parts in the top bar, then Inventory in the left menu), on the Active tab.
custom_steps:
1. Click New Inventory Part.
  2. Type a description for part A in the Description field.
  3. Press Tab.
  4. Type part A's part number.
  5. Pick any category in the Category field.
  6. Type 10.00 in the Cost field.
  7. Click Save.
  8. Type part A's part number in the Search box.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • A window titled "New Inventory Part" opens.
  • Its first field is Description and the next field is Part Number.
  • There is no Part Library (or Catalog Part) field anywhere in the window, and no lookup list opens.

Step 2:

  • The Description field holds the text as typed.

Step 3:

  • The cursor moves to the Part Number field.

Step 4:

  • Part Number holds part A's part number as plain typed text, with no list to pick from.

Step 5:

  • The category shows in the Category field.

Step 6:

  • Cost reads $10.00.

Step 7:

  • The window closes and the part is saved: no Part Library step was asked for.

Step 8:

  • One row is listed, with part A's description and part number.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 33 (23 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10820 (Story 7, Create a Part by Typing Its Number and Description)

  • S7-R1: “The New Inventory Part dialog has a Description field, followed by a Part Number field. Both are free text.”
  • S7-R2: “The dialog has no Part Library selector and no Part Library lookup step.”
  • Feature Overview, Core functionality: “Creating a part takes a part number and a description typed straight into the part dialog. The system links the part to the Part Library in the background.”
